Class NumberUtils

java.lang.Object
net.emustudio.emulib.runtime.helpers.NumberUtils
@ThreadSafe public final class NumberUtils extends Object

  • Method Details

    • reverseBits

      public static int reverseBits(int value, int numberOfBits)
      Reverse bits in integer (max 32-bit) value.
      Parameters:
      value - value which bits will be reversed
      numberOfBits - how many bits should be reversed. If the value has more bits, the rest will be preserved.
      Returns:
      value with reversed bits

    • reverseBits

      public static long reverseBits(long value, int numberOfBits)
      Reverse bits in long (max 64-bit) value.

      Unlike reverseBits(int, int), higher bits of value are discarded (not preserved), and numberOfBits <= 0 yields 0.

      Parameters:
      value - value which bits will be reversed
      numberOfBits - how many lowest bits should be reversed
      Returns:
      value with the lowest numberOfBits bits reversed and higher bits cleared

    • readBits

      public static int readBits(byte[] bytes, int start, int length, int strategy)
      Reads an arbitrary number of bits (max 32) from bytes.

      If the strategy is LITTLE_ENDIAN, bits are read from LSB to MSB. If it is BIG_ENDIAN, bits are read from MSB to LSB.

      Parameters:
      bytes - bytes
      start - the bit index where reading starts
      length - the number of bits to read
      strategy - combination of NumberUtils.Strategy flags
      Returns:
      the bits read

    • readInt

      public static int readInt(Number[] word, int strategy)
      Combines up to 4 memory cells into an integer.

      Each cell represents one byte; higher-order bits of a cell are cut. If there are more than 4 cells, only the first 4 are used. If there are fewer, the missing most significant bytes are zero.

      Parameters:
      word - the cells (e.g. Byte[], Short[] or Integer[])
      strategy - combination of NumberUtils.Strategy flags
      Returns:
      32-bit value

    • writeInt

      public static void writeInt(int value, Byte[] output, int strategy)
      Splits an integer into 4 bytes. It is the inverse of readInt(Number[], int).
      Parameters:
      value - the value
      output - the output; must have space for 4 bytes. Other elements are untouched.
      strategy - combination of NumberUtils.Strategy flags
